clue.text: Nose to nose, perhaps, and ready

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the words could be arranged some other way, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Two people standing nose to nose, squaring up and ready for a confrontation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' tells you to rearrange all ten letters of NOSE TO NOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alert and prepared for action is the idiomatic sense of standing poised on tiptoe.

clue.text: English name, no French one

parts.note: taken as written
un is the French word for one

explanation.surface: An English name that has no French counterpart.
explanation.definitionFit: In English grammar a noun is a naming word, the part of speech that names things.

clue.text: I follow uncle around the centres

indicators.note: follow places the letter I after the rearranged uncle
around suggests the letters of uncle are turned about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone trailing an uncle around the town centres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges UNCLE to NUCLE, and 'follow' puts I after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclei is the plural of nucleus, a core or central point.

clue.text: A little bit of heaven?

parts.note: a fraction such as one part in seven is a little bit, and the phrase for supreme bliss pairs that ordinal with heaven

explanation.definitionFit: The expression for ecstatic happiness is the ordinal after sixth followed by heaven, and that ordinal also names a fraction.

clue.text: Don't lie under it

parts.note: a witness who has sworn in court is under a solemn promise and must tell the truth

explanation.definitionFit: A sworn promise in court binds a witness to truthfulness, so you must not lie while under one.

clue.text: Meeting that has no standing?

parts.note: a meeting is also called a sitting, so everyone in it is seated rather than standing

explanation.definitionFit: A formal sitting of a council or court is a period of meeting, and sitting is the opposite of standing.

clue.text: Pop-singer's dreadfully overbearing

indicators.note: dreadfully signals the letters are badly mangled into a new order

parts.note: all ten letters, including the final S, are the fodder

explanation.surface: A pop singer's dreadful arrogance, overbearing to all around.
explanation.definitionFit: Crushing others with harsh authority is a domineering, tyrannical manner.

clue.text: House calls may double a salesman's objective

indicators.note: double means the word for the salesman's goal is written out twice

parts.note: a salesman aims to win an order from the customer

explanation.surface: Door-to-door visits may double what a salesman hopes to achieve.
explanation.walkthrough: The House is the House of Commons, where the Speaker calls for quiet with a repeated cry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Speaker of the Commons restores quiet by shouting this repeated cry, an example of calls in that chamber.

clue.text: Mast bearing standard

parts.note: S, for south, is a compass bearing
par is the standard or normal level

explanation.surface: A ship's mast that carries a flag or standard.
explanation.definitionFit: A pole used as a mast, boom or yard on a ship is a nautical spar.

clue.text: Russian capitalists

parts.note: read not as money-makers but as people who live in Russia's capital city

explanation.definitionFit: Residents of Moscow, the Russian capital, are literally the people of that capital.

clue.text: Spares may be few and far between

indicators.note: may be hints that the letters could form some other word when rearranged

explanation.surface: Spare parts can be hard to come by.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinly scattered and scarce is the meaning of the idiom about rarity.

clue.text: More than one player is in new boots

indicators.note: in places the little word is inside the rearranged boots
new indicates the letters of boots are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A footballer wearing new boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns BOOTS into OBOTS, and 'in' puts IS inside it, after OBO.
explanation.definitionFit: Players of a woodwind instrument with a double reed are musicians, plural, so more than one player.

clue.text: Expanding, becoming more communicative

explanation.surface: A shy person blossoming and becoming chattier.
explanation.definitionFit: Spreading wider is one sense and growing less reserved and more talkative is the figurative one.

clue.text: Just fancy!

parts.note: looks like an exclamation of surprise but describes something merely decorative, fancy rather than useful

explanation.definitionFit: Something purely decorative serves only for show, which is what just fancy describes.

clue.text: Maker of ropes or sails

indicators.note: or offers an alternative, here an alternative arrangement of the letters of sails

explanation.surface: Someone who makes ropes or sails for ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a weak signal: read it as 'alternatively', so the letters of SAILS are put in another order.
explanation.definitionFit: This fibre from an agave plant is the material twine and cordage are made from.

clue.text: Gets as far as waking up?

explanation.surface: A question about how far someone gets when they wake.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching a point is one sense, and regaining consciousness after fainting is the other.

clue.text: Where people involved with rackets may be seen, in more than one way

definitions.text: Where people involved with rackets may be seen, in more than one way

parts.words: Where people involved with rackets may be seen, in more than one way
parts.note: rackets are both tennis bats and criminal schemes, so players and crooks each end up in a place with this name

explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is played on one and criminals are tried in another, so both kinds of racket meet there.

clue.text: Unexpectedly met with a greeting, not returned

parts.note: hi is a casual greeting

indicators.note: returned means the little word not is read backwards

explanation.surface: Surprised by a greeting that was not returned.
explanation.definitionFit: To find or come upon something by chance is a phrasal verb meaning stumbled upon.

clue.text: A feature of Sicily and French North Africa

parts.note: the clue's French and is et in French
NA is an abbreviation for North Africa

explanation.surface: Something found in Sicily and in French North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' goes with the 'and' before it: the French word for and is ET.
explanation.definitionFit: The great volcano on Sicily's east coast is the island's best-known landmark.

clue.text: Pirate said to practise deception

indicators.note: said shows the word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to kid is to fool or tease

explanation.surface: A pirate rumoured to be a trickster.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain William Kidd was a notorious seventeenth-century Scottish pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain William Kidd was a famous privateer turned buccaneer.

clue.text: Scotsman backs an alternative instruction for computers

parts.note: Mac is a nickname for a Scotsman, from the common surname prefix

indicators.note: backs means the next word is turned to read the other way

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A Scot backing another method of programming.
explanation.definitionFit: A single command standing for a sequence of computer operations is a programming shortcut.

clue.text: Person in Italian society breaking the rules

definitions.text: Person in Italian society breaking the rules

parts.words: Person in Italian society breaking the rules
parts.note: society here is the secret criminal organisation of Sicily, whose members live outside the law

explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Sicilian criminal brotherhood is a lawbreaker in that Italian society.

clue.text: Employment of paper folders

parts.note: folders suggests office files, but means people who fold paper as a craft

explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese art of folding sheets into shapes is what such craftspeople practise.

clue.text: I'm holding a number said to be corrupt

indicators.note: holding means the first word has another inside it

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
oral means spoken

explanation.surface: A claim that I'm keeping a figure that is corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts M inside IM to give IMM; ORAL follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Morally depraved conduct is wicked, lacking any ethical principles.

clue.text: How happy cowboys might be?

parts.note: gunslingers eager to shoot are described with the word for a gun's firing lever plus happy

explanation.definitionFit: Being quick to fire a gun is called by a compound of the firing lever and happy.

clue.text: Yet his talk is far from uplifting!

definitions.text: Yet his talk is far from uplifting!

parts.words: Yet his talk is far from uplifting!
parts.note: a balloon's envelope lifts it into the air, but a windbag who chatters endlessly is tiresome

explanation.definitionFit: An endlessly talkative person is called a windbag, the same term as a balloon's gas envelope.

clue.text: He was partly known for his fasting and his leadership

definitions.text: He was partly known for his fasting and his leadership

indicators.note: partly means only part of the letters of these words is used

explanation.surface: An Indian leader famed for hunger strikes and leadership.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian independence leader Mahatma was famous for hunger strikes and leading non-violent resistance.

clue.text: Sort of wolves apparently extinct?

explanation.surface: A kind of wolf that seems to have died out.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix for man-wolves of legend is one sense, and the past tense of are suggests no longer existing.

clue.text: She was a copper, once, in Bombay

explanation.surface: A woman who was once a police officer in Bombay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like slang for a police officer, but it is a copper coin: the old Indian coin worth one sixteenth of a rupee.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name is one sense; the other is a former Indian coin of low value.

clue.text: A singular display of musical virtuosity

definitions.text: A singular display of musical virtuosity

parts.words: A singular display of musical virtuosity
parts.note: singular means remarkable, but also one person: a street performer playing several instruments alone

explanation.definitionFit: A busker who plays several instruments at once performs as a solo ensemble.

clue.text: State of a hut that needs putting in order

indicators.note: the jumbled letters need rearranging into the right order

explanation.surface: The state of a hut needing a tidy-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A western American state, home to Salt Lake City.

clue.text: He's the first to take over

definitions.text: He's the first to take over

parts.words: He's the first to take over
parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls, and one of the two batsmen starting the innings faces the first

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled from one end; the batsman who starts the innings faces them first.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer who begins the innings faces the first balls bowled, so is first to face an over.
